items.title: 25 Flatbush Avenue
items.excerpt: Five-storey commercial loft with a bracketed metal cornice, masonry piers, stone bands, broad second-storey glazing and upper sash windows. The lot 24 photograph is a substitute card. The loft appears in views from neighboring lots 26 and 19. The later building survey height is an approximate roofline reference. Period storefront finishes, the construction system, and the extent of the 1989 alteration are uncertain.

items.title: NYC Department of Buildings, certificate of occupancy 231396, 25 April 1989 (both sides)
items.excerpt: Certificate 231396 for 19–27 Flatbush records three stores and offices on floors 2–5 after the alteration completed 24 March 1989. It lists a height of 45 ft, while a later building footprint survey gives 69.87 ft. The figures disagree. The certificate gives no storefront names or finishes.

items.title: City of New York, April 1996 orthophotography, NYC Ortho 1996 Mosaic (after the reconstruction date)
items.excerpt: The orthophoto mosaic is useful for cross-checking street alignment, the block outline, and the relationship of the loft and bank to the parking gap. It was taken six years after the target year and cannot establish 1990 storefronts or whether disputed 1990 structures were still standing.

items.title: 1 Flatbush Avenue
items.excerpt: Low corner restaurant with a clipped prow, strip windows, projecting striped fascia and paired pole signs. Evidence limitations: Sign wording is legible in the photograph; the 1993 permit corroborates the owner, not the exact sign design in 1990.

items.title: 15-17 Flatbush Avenue
items.excerpt: Two-storey commercial infill with broad upper windows, a flat coping and shopfronts. Evidence limitations: Separate old footprint between the restaurant and the taller loft. Signs and the rear return are incompletely resolved.

items.title: 560 Fulton Street (later 570)
items.excerpt: Three-storey industrial loft, five wide factory-window bays in a pale masonry frame, dark spandrels, shallow cornice and low shopfront band. Evidence limitations: Photo title is 560 Fulton. Matched by block and lot 35; later redevelopment address is 570. No modern tower is used.

items.title: 572 Fulton Street
items.excerpt: Narrow three-storey shop, four segment-headed upper openings across, cornice, exposed plain end wall. Evidence limitations: Disputed. A 1980s photo and a 1992 full-demolition filing identify a 30 ft, three-storey building on lot 40. A 2008 archaeological report reading the 1969, 1979 and 1989 Sanborn sheets instead calls the lot parking. Model gives priority to photograph and DOB for existence, using the report's 22 by 40 ft historic dimensions only as a provisional size. View this as a hypothesis.

items.title: 33-35 Flatbush Avenue
items.excerpt: Restrained neoclassical bank and office loft; six window axes on the upper floors, round-headed top surrounds and a two-level glazed base. Evidence limitations: Seven visible levels: five over the two-level base. Modern PLUTO counts eight; the photo governs the street elevation. No later movie-set bank name shown.

items.title: Pioneer Warehouses / 41 Flatbush Avenue
items.excerpt: Romanesque Revival commercial storage complex; broad buff-brick elevation, small dark openings alternating with blind recesses, masonry base, arched entry, ships' prows and dated urns. Evidence limitations: Modeled before the 2010s office conversion, with blocked openings rather than the present large glazing. Four construction campaigns commemorated: 1896, 1902, 1910, 1914.

items.excerpt: Six-storey piano factory with broad industrial sash groups above a glazed showroom. Evidence limitations: Height estimated from period photo and adjoining cornice; excludes the six-floor residential addition documented in 2007. The modern 171 ft height must not be used.

items.title: 59 Flatbush Avenue
items.excerpt: Narrow matching white or light-painted loft face, multi-light factory sash, deep shop window and furniture sign. Evidence limitations: Four small-window upper rows over a showroom and shop read as six levels in the photograph. Cornice steps near the piano factory. Period roof height estimated; later survey records 86 ft and PLUTO seven floors.

items.title: 38 Flatbush Avenue
items.excerpt: Triangular postwar office block with horizontal ribbon windows, solid corner piers and recessed dark base, opposite the older lofts. Evidence limitations: Current outline and height used as proxies; banding follows the tax image rather than later renovations. The Fox Theatre that occupied this block was demolished in 1971.
